channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Quaest: Flavio oscila pra cima; vantagem numérica de Lula cai nos 2 turnos
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro increased in voting intentions in both first and second round scenarios, within the margin of error, while President Lula decreased but still holds a lead.

item.title: Lula tem 44% ante 39% de Flávio no 2º turno, diz Quaest
item.description: Lula leads the runoff with 44% voting intention against 39% for Flávio Bolsonaro, according to the Genial/Quaest poll from August 2026, maintaining a stable lead since July. Lula's government has 48% approval and 47% disapproval, while 54% of voters reject Flávio Bolsonaro and 52% reject Lula. The economy remains a key concern, with 43% believing it worsened over the past 12 months, but 46% expecting improvement in the coming year.

item.title: O que diz a nova pesquisa Meio/Ideia sobre a disputa entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The latest Meio/Ideia poll shows Lula leading with 48.5% against Flávio Bolsonaro's 43% in a hypothetical 2026 runoff, though the margin of error technically ties Bolsonaro with Ronaldo Caiado at 40%. In the first round, Lula leads with 43%, eight points ahead of Bolsonaro's 35%.

item.title: Meio/Ideia: Flávio é rejeitado por 48% e Lula, por 47,4%
item.description: The Meio/Ideia poll conducted from July 31 to August 3, 2026 shows that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) is rejected by 48% of voters, while President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) has 47.4% rejection, indicating a near technical tie in disapproval. Romeu Zema (Novo) ranks third with 14.6% rejection. The survey interviewed 1,500 people, has a margin of error of 2.5 percentage points, and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Meio/Ideia: Lula é desaprovado por 49% contra 48,5% que o aprovam
item.description: A Meio/Ideia poll released on August 5, 2026, shows 49% of voters disapprove of President Lula’s work, while 48,5% approve, within a 2.5-point margin of error. Approval rose from 46.5% in July to 48.5%, while disapproval stayed at 48.5%, indicating a slight improvement in public perception. Additionally, 36.6% rate the government as excellent or good, 24% as fair, and 37% as poor or terrible.

item.title: Governo Lula é aprovado por 48% e desaprovado por 47%, diz Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll from August 2026 shows a technical tie in approval of Lula’s government, with 48% approving and 47% disapproving, within the margin of error. In a hypothetical second-round scenario, Lula leads with 44% voting intention against Flávio Bolsonaro’s 39%, while both candidates face high rejection rates (52% and 54%). Government evaluation is split: 36% positive, 26% regular, and 36% negative.

item.title: Saiba o que os candidatos e pré-candidatos ao Planalto farão nesta 4ª
item.description: On Wednesday, August 5, 2026, presidential candidates maintained pre-campaign agendas, including interviews, legislative signings, and sector-specific meetings. Lula signed PLV 6/2026 on freight policies, gave podcast interviews, and met with truckers about the Move Brazil program. Flávio Bolsonaro announced his running mate in an interview at Teatro Juca Chaves, while Ronaldo Caiado attended the state convention in Goiânia. Other candidates, such as Renan Santos and Augusto Cury, fulfilled regional agendas involving media interviews and sectoral events.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Lula venceria Flávio Bolsonaro por 39% a 30% no 1º turno e 44% a 39% no 2º turno
item.description: A Genial/Quaest poll released on April 5, 2026 shows President Lula (PT) leading Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) with 39% to 30% in the first round and 44% to 39% in the second round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election. The results indicate a consistent advantage for the PT candidate in both scenarios.

item.title: Lula tem vantagem sobre Flávio no 2º turno, aponta Meio Ideia
item.description: Lula maintains an advantage over Flávio Bolsonaro in a simulated runoff for the 2026 election, according to a Meio Ideia poll released on November 5, 2026. The president leads the senator in voting projections.

item.title: Escolha de Girão como vice de Zema é boa notícia para... Ciro Gomes
item.description: The selection of Eduardo Girão as Romeu Zema's running mate in the presidential ticket is seen as positive news for Ciro Gomes, the gubernatorial candidate in Ceará, as it removes a right-wing contender who was splitting his voter base. With Girão no longer in the race for the Ceará government, his 3% polling share may shift to Ciro, potentially enabling a first-round victory over Elmano de Freitas (PT), although Elmano's allies downplay the electoral impact.

item.title: Genial/ Quaest: Lula lidera 1º e 2º turnos, mas Flávio cresce
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows Lula leading the first round with 39% and the second round with 44%, while Flávio Bolsonaro rises to 30% in the first round and 39% in the second. Lula lost one percentage point in both rounds since July, while Flávio gained two points in each. Blank, null, and non-voters total 13%, and undecided voters are 4%.

item.title: Marqueteiro de Flávio provoca Lula por criticar agressão a mulheres: ‘Perdeu o voto do filho’
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's newly hired marketer, Duda Lima, provoked Lula by claiming the president 'lost his statements on his son, Lula lost his own son's vote after criticizing men who assault women, referencing a domestic violence accusation against Lula's youngest son, Luís Cláudio. The Bolsonaro campaign, under Lima's direction, has deployed AI-generated videos to highlight perceived contradictions in Lula's stance on gender-based violence and intensified corruption allegations involving Lula's other sons, including Fábio Luís (Lulinha) and Marcola, former chief of staff.

item.title: Isolado, Flávio Bolsonaro deve ir de Rogério Marinho como vice
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is expected to announce Rogério Marinho as his vice-presidential running mate today, following Marinho's role as political coordinator of his campaign. The senator is considered the strong favorite for the position, barring any last-minute changes. The information is exclusive to subscribers of the outlet that published the report.

item.title: Lula e os debates
item.description: A survey of 1.562 readers found that 41.7% believe Lula should not attend presidential debates, while 37% support his participation and 21.3% say he should only attend if he wants to. The issue reflects divisions over the former president’s stance ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Dark Horse: Ancine detecta irregularidade e indica multa para produtora
item.description: Brazil's National Cinema Agency (Ancine) has fined producer Go Up Entertainment for irregularities in the filming of 'Dark Horse', a movie depicting former President Jair Bolsonaro's political trajectory. The film sparked controversy after leaked messages showed Senator Flávio Bolsonaro allegedly demanding money from Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro to finance the production.

item.title: Jogos de hoje, quarta, 5 de agosto: onde assistir futebol ao vivo e horários
item.description: On Wednesday, August 5, 2026, the Copa do Brasil features four decisive round-of-16 matches, highlighted by the Fluminense-Vasco derby at Maracanã after a 0-0 draw in the first leg. Palmeiras holds a comfortable advantage over Fortaleza, able to lose by up to two goals and still advance. Earlier, international friendlies with Manchester City, Chelsea, Juventus, PSG, and Arsenal took place in the morning and afternoon, alongside Champions League qualifiers between Fenerbahçe and Sturm Graz and an Argentine league match.

item.title: Estadão lança projeto ‘Carrapatos’ para fortalecer cobertura da eleição à Presidência da República
item.description: Estadão launched the 'Carrapatos' project to deepen digital coverage of the 2026 presidential campaigns, with reporters following Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in video. The initiative highlights both candidates’ long media presence since Lula’s 1975 union leadership and Flávio’s 2003 state deputy debut, reinforcing the newspaper’s decades-long political coverage.

item.title: De sindicalista a preso na Lava Jato: ‘carrapato’ conta a trajetória de Lula em busca de 4º mandato
item.description: Estadão launches the 'Carrapatos' project to track Lula's campaign for a fourth presidential term, highlighting his journey from union leader in 1979 to imprisonment in the Lava Jato operation and subsequent annulments by the STF. The piece covers his first metalworkers' strike, the founding of the PT, six presidential runs, and his first victory in 2002, with emphasis on initiatives like Fome Zero and scandals such as the mensalão. Reporter Levy Teles will follow Lula as the designated 'carrapato' for this new electoral cycle.

item.title: De deputado da ‘rachadinha’ a sucessor de Jair: ‘caparrato’ conta a trajetória de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, a state deputy for 23 years and son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, is running for president in 2026 after a career marked by conservative stances, defense of the military dictatorship, involvement in the 'rachadinha' scandal with Fabrício Queiroz, and a strong focus on public security. His campaign now seeks to broaden alliances, win over female voters, and harden crime-fighting policies, while Estadão launches the 'Carrapatos' project to provide deep digital coverage of his presidential bid.

item.title: Advogado da amiga de Lulinha defende nova estratégia de atuação
item.description: Lawyer Roberto Podval has taken over as the sole defender of businesswoman Roberta Luchsinger, friend of Lulinha, after Bruno Salles left the defense team. He advocates for a non-politicized legal approach, avoiding clashes with the PF, STF, and MP, insisting the case should be handled in court, not in the public sphere.

item.title: Argentina critica redução de representação diplomática do Brasil
item.description: Argentina criticized Brazil's decision to downgrade bilateral diplomatic representation, accusing the Brazilian government of isolating itself regionally for purely ideological reasons. The move followed repeated insults by Argentine President Javier Milei against Brazilian authorities, including President Lula and Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, during political events and interviews. Brazil responded by keeping its ambassador Julio Bitelli in Brasília until Milei ceases the offenses, appointing minister-counselor Eduardo Uziel as chargé d'affaires in Buenos Aires.

item.title: Quem é o responsável pelas madeixas de nomes como Jão, o ator Felipe Heráclito Lima e o governador Eduardo Leite
item.description: Singer Jão, actor Felipe Heráclito Lima, and Rio Grande do Sul governor Eduardo Leite are all clients of hairstylist Renan Gallardo, who works at the Casa Conceito Jardins salon in São Paulo. Despite their different fields — music, theater, and politics — they share the same beauty professional and frequent the same location in Jardim Europa. Gallardo, with over 160k Instagram followers, is known for serving celebrities, influencers, and high-end liberal professionals.

item.title: Governo avalia rever exigência de CNPJ e nota fiscal para ‘nanoempreendedor’ diante de risco político
item.description: The federal government is reviewing the requirement for nanoentrepreneurs to obtain a CNPJ and issue invoices, a rule introduced via decree as part of the Tax Reform, due to growing political risk. The mandate, which forces informal workers to formalize despite not being subject to CBS and IBS taxes, has sparked resistance and low compliance. A potential reversal aims to avoid electoral wear ahead of municipal elections and the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Pizzolato e Cerveró aparecem em lista de contas irregulares do TCU
item.description: Former Banco do Brasil director Henrique Pizzolato and former Petrobras director Nestor Cerveró were included in the TCU's list of irregular accounts forwarded to the TSE, with ineligibility recorded until October 2029 and April 2029, respectively. The list also includes filmmaker Tizuka Yamasaki, ineligible until February 2031 due to unverified use of funds from the Rouanet and Audiovisual Laws. The document, containing over 6,1 thousand names, supports the TSE's analysis of ineligibility under the Clean Record Law.

item.title: Paralisação de trens entra no segundo dia e põe concessões no centro da disputa eleitoral em São Paulo
item.description: The strike by CPTM workers, now in its second day, has suspended service on lines 11-Coral, 12-Safira, and 13-Jade, disrupting commutes for thousands in the São Paulo metropolitan area and intensifying the electoral debate over public transport concessions. The opposition criticizes the private sector's performance in transportation and other state services, putting Governor Tarcísio de Freitas at the center of the controversy, while he defends the concession model as efficient and essential for modernization.

item.title: Isolado, Flávio terá mais de um minuto a menos de tempo de TV que Lula na campanha presidencial
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) will have 4 minutes and 20 seconds of TV time per electoral propaganda block, while President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will have 5 minutes and 32 seconds — a difference of 1 minute and 12 seconds per program. This disparity stems from Flávio’s partisan isolation, as he failed to form coalitions, unlike Lula, who is backed by six parties and federations. Nevertheless, the PL’s bench of 98 federal deputies ensures Flávio a substantial share of free airtime under the proportional distribution rule established by electoral law.

item.title: Ex-hater de Tarcísio: quem é o suplente de André do Prado após saída de Eduardo
item.description: Following Eduardo Bolsonaro's ineligibility, André do Prado (PL) selected Fernando Fiori de Godoy (PL), former mayor of Holambra, as his first alternate for the São Paulo Senate race. Fiori de Godoy, who is currently on Tarcísio de Freitas's ticket, had previously criticized the governor in 2022, supporting Rodrigo Garcia and appearing alongside Geraldo Alckmin. Despite the current alliance, his past opposition to Tarcísio raises political interest.

item.title: Filhos de Tarcísio criam empresa de consultoria empresarial
item.description: In February 2026, the sons of São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas founded Ferreira de Freitas Participações Ltda., a microenterprise with R$10,000 capital and headquarters in Barueri. In June 2026, the company partnered with RB Par Ltda. (BA) to form BR Invest Participações Ltda., whose main activity is holding stakes in other companies, according to the Federal Revenue. Rodrigo Barbosa de Sousa, a partner in BR Invest, has family ties to Lex Tax, a tax consulting firm serving major São Paulo corporations.

item.title: Buenos Aires diz que Brasil pediu saída do embaixador argentino
item.description: Brazil has requested the return of Argentina’s ambassador to Buenos Aires, according to the Argentine government, in response to critical remarks by President Javier Milei against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The move comes amid a deepening diplomatic rift between the two nations. The request reflects Brazil’s dissatisfaction with what it views as offensive statements from the Argentine leader.

item.title: Frei Betto: "Esquerda brasileira está igual à seleção depois da derrrota para a Noruega"
item.description: Frei Betto criticized the Brazilian left for failing to innovate, abandoning grassroots work, and losing touch with popular sectors, comparing it to the Brazilian national team after its defeat to Norway in the 2026 World Cup. He also noted that the left does not dominate the digital space, where the right holds hegemony and produces more impactful content, leaving progressives in a reactive position.

item.title: Fantasma da corrupção abala fase de calmaria de Lula
item.description: The approaching start of the 2026 electoral campaign ended a period of calm around Lula, following the resurgence of the Master case and the inclusion of his closest advisor in corruption investigations. The 'ghost of corruption' is once again haunting the government, creating tension in the Planalto Palace.

item.title: Brasil retira a su embajador en Argentina en rechazo a los insultos de Milei contra Lula
item.description: The Brazilian government recalled its ambassador from Argentina and downgraded bilateral relations in response to repeated personal insults by Argentine President Javier Milei against Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. This marks the worst diplomatic incident between the two countries since the 1980s democratization, undermining the core of Mercosur, formed by Latin America’s two largest economies.

item.title: ¿Hasta qué punto ayuda Trump a Bolsonaro?
item.description: The article analyzes how a potential victory by Flávio Bolsonaro over Lula in the 2026 Brazilian elections could consolidate Donald Trump’s influence over South America, turning the region into an extension of his personal interests. It emphasizes that Brazil, due to its size and resources, is strategic to this ambition, and that the electoral campaign, officially starting on August 16, unfolds under the threat of foreign interference for the first time since Brazil’s redemocratization in the 1980s.

item.title: Argentina diz que Brasil rebaixou relações por "questões ideológicas"
item.description: Argentina criticized Brazil for downgrading diplomatic relations, calling Lula's decision motivated by 'purely ideological reasons'. The Javier Milei government claims Brazil is isolating itself from the region and states that Argentina has never turned political disagreements into diplomatic incidents, maintaining a foreign policy based on national interest and sovereignty. The downgrade follows repeated attacks by Milei against Lula, Minister Alexandre de Moraes, and Brazilian institutions, prompting Itamaraty to reduce relations to the level of chargés d'affaires.

item.title: Oposição culpa Lula por revogação de visto de embaixadora nos EUA
item.description: Opposition politicians blamed the Lula administration for the revocation of the Brazilian ambassador's visa in the U.S., Maria Luiza Viotti, in retaliation for delays in approving Trump's nominee. Flávio Bolsonaro accused the government of incompetence and rancor, while Eduardo Bolsonaro attributed the move to Lula's ego. Government supporters condemned the U.S. decision as interference and blackmail, defending Brazil's firm stance.

item.title: Presidente desperdiça a campanha
item.description: Lula spoke for 62 minutes in a PT meeting but delivered little substance, announcing only five generic commitments: education, elderly programs, military industry, rare earths for Brazilians, and energy transition. The critique argues he wasted a chance to define a clear campaign brand amid a government perceived as lacking strong identity. The subscriber-only article suggests a lack of strategic direction in political communication.

item.title: g1 e GloboNews entrevistam Renan Santos, candidato à Presidência, nesta quarta; saiba como assistir
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate for the Missão party, will be interviewed by journalists Andréia Sadi and Natuza Nery on g1 and GloboNews this Wednesday (5) at 2 p.m., with simultaneous live broadcast. The interview is part of a series featuring the top five candidates from the July 24 Datafolha poll, following a draw that determined the order of appearances. After airing, the full content will be available as video on g1 and audio on the 'O Assunto' podcast.

item.title: Na pré-campanha, presidenciáveis usam IA em jingles, sátiras, cenas fictícias e ataques
item.description: In the 2026 pre-campaign, artificial intelligence is being used to produce videos, jingles, and satirical content featuring candidates in fictional scenarios, such as Lula with an AI-generated voice, Flávio Bolsonaro as a fighter jet pilot, and Renan Santos attacking Daniel Vorcaro. According to the IA in Elections Observatory, 45% of such content is classified as misleading and 73% lacks disclosure of AI use, raising concerns about disinformation as the election approaches.

item.title: Convenções partidárias vão até esta quarta-feira; entenda os próximos passos
item.description: Party conventions for the 2026 Brazilian elections end this Wednesday (5), formalizing candidacies for Lula (PT), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Romeu Zema (Novo) and Renan Santos (Missão). Candidacy registration must be completed by 7 p.m. on August 15, with the official campaign starting on August 16. The first round is scheduled for October 4, and a potential runoff for major offices on October 25.

item.title: Lula sanciona hoje MP que aumenta fiscalização da tabela do frete; entenda o que muda
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed a provisional measure expanding the ANTT's authority to monitor and penalize non-compliance with the minimum freight table, barring companies that violate it from hiring cargo transport. The measure aims to secure a minimum freight rate for truckers amid rising diesel prices, factoring in distance, vehicle type, cargo nature, and operational costs. It also strengthens the Procargas program by prioritizing fleet renewal, rest stops, professional training, and financial access for cargo transporters.

item.title: Lula recebe motoristas de aplicativo em meio a trava em programa de crédito para compra de carros
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva met with ride-hailing drivers at the Planalto Palace, just over a month after launching the Move Brasil program, which offers automobile financing for taxi and app-based drivers. The meeting took place amid challenges in implementing the program, which faces operational and credit access obstacles. The gathering aims to adjust the program to the category’s needs, though no specific agreements were disclosed.

item.title: Aliados de Lula veem revogação de visto como nova tentativa de Trump de interferir nas eleições e vão insistir em discurso de soberania
item.description: Lula's allies view the U.S. revocation of the visa for Brazil's ambassador to the U.S., Maria Luiza Viotti, as a political move by Trump to interfere in Brazil's 2026 presidential election, calling the justification false and retaliatory. They link the action to Trump's support for the Bolsonaro clan, particularly Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, and see it as grounds to accuse the opposition of undermining Brazilian sovereignty.

item.title: Lula sanciona nesta quarta proposta que estabelece novas regras para frete rodoviário
item.description: President Lula signed into law a proposal that changes the rules for the minimum road freight floor, maintaining the requirement for a minimum but removing Congress's authority to set specific values. The measure increases penalties for companies that fail to pay the floor, currently calculated by the ANTT based on distance, number of axles, and cargo type, and includes amnesty for fines imposed on truckers for 2022 protests, although the Ministry of Transport recommended vetoing this and other provisions.

item.title: O que esperar da Bolsa no período eleitoral? Analistas preveem 'mar revolto' até outubro
item.description: The São Paulo Stock Exchange (B3) recorded positive foreign capital inflows in July, with R$ 2.1 billion for the month and R$ 36 billion year-to-date, reversing three months of outflows. Analysts identify three factors that could boost the Ibovespa through end-2025: reduced exposure to overseas tech stocks, easing fears about Middle East conflict consequences, and the view that Brazilian equities are now 'discounted,' trading at 8.3x earnings — below the historical average of 10.5x. However, the electoral period is expected to create market volatility through December, with political uncertainty affecting interest rate forecasts and asset pricing.

item.title: Justiça Eleitoral manda Lula abrir gastos com publicidade
item.description: TSE Minister André Mendonça ordered the Lula government to submit, within 10 days, all documentation on institutional advertising expenses from 2023 to June 2026, following a claim by the Liberal Party (PL). The PL alleges the government exceeded legal spending limits on advertising in 2026, citing R$178 million committed by June — allegedly R$42.3 million above the cap — and highlights campaigns like the New PAC, COP30, and workweek reform as improper government self-promotion during an election year.

item.title: Governo Lula rebaixa nível da relação diplomática com a Argentina
item.description: The Lula government downgraded diplomatic relations with Argentina following repeated insults by Argentine President Javier Milei against Brazilian authorities, including President Lula and Minister Alexandre de Moraes. Brazil's ambassador to Buenos Aires, Julio Bitelli, will remain in Brazil until Milei ceases his attacks, with Minister-Counselor Eduardo Uziel acting as interim replacement. The move was confirmed by Itamaraty and also affects Argentina's ambassador to Brazil, Daniel Raimondi, whose stay depends on Milei's decision.

item.title: Alta da dívida gera pressão de aliados para que Lula defenda ajuste fiscal na campanha
item.description: PT allies intensified pressure on President Lula to publicly commit to maintaining the fiscal framework in a potential fourth term, amid rising public debt. The proposal aims to ensure economic stability and counter pressure from conservative sectors and financial markets.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro culpam governo Lula por rejeição do centrão e miram 2º turno
item.description: Allies of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) claim that his political isolation — due to the lack of support from other parties — stems from pressure exerted by President Lula’s (PT) government on the centrão, not from his own poor articulation skills. They argue the federal government actively blocked potential alliances to weaken his candidacy. This narrative shifts blame for failed negotiations onto the executive branch.

item.title: Lula vira alvo de rivais, mas mantém na campanha assessor que pegou empréstimo de amiga de Lulinha
item.description: President Lula (PT) became a target of political rivals after it was revealed that one of his closest advisors received a loan from a businesswoman who is a friend of his son, Lulinha, and under investigation by the Federal Police. Despite electoral backlash and conflict-of-interest allegations, Lula chose to retain the advisor in his campaign team, signaling a preference for personal loyalty over political or media pressure.

item.title: PL escolhe vereadora de Niterói para ser vice de Douglas Ruas no Rio
item.description: Douglas Ruas, the PL candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro, announced Niterói councilwoman Fernanda Louback (PL) as his running mate for vice-governor, completing the ticket on the eve of the deadline for party conventions. Fernanda, an atypical mother and advocate for people with disabilities and autism, is abandoning her pre-candidacy for state deputy to run for the Guanabara Palace. The announcement follows ruptures with PP and União Brasil, prompting the PL to form a 'pure-blood' ticket in the state.
